sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *cuando* and *mientras* from A2 Unit 13. *Cuando* introduces what happens at a moment; *mientras* introduces what is going on at the same time as something else. Together they tell how a caudillo raised and dissolved his forces.

sections.title: Two ways to link actions
rows: Cuando necesitaba soldados, reclutaba a los hombres.
*cuando* = at the moment when: when he needed soldiers
Mientras duraba la guerra, los hombres seguían al jefe.
*mientras* + imperfect = during the whole time: while the war lasted
Quiroga regresaba de un viaje cuando lo atacaron.
imperfect for what was going on, *cuando* + preterite for the event that interrupts

items.spanish: Cuando terminaba la guerra, los hombres volvían a su trabajo.
items.english: When the war ended, the men went back to their work.

items.spanish: Mientras el jefe vivía, los hombres lo obedecían.
items.english: While the chief was alive, the men obeyed him.

items.spanish: Cuando terminó la guerra, el caudillo disolvió sus fuerzas.
items.english: When the war ended, the caudillo dissolved his forces.

items.spanish: Los jinetes llegaban a caballo mientras el jefe esperaba.
items.english: The horsemen arrived on horseback while the chief waited.

sections.content: Use the imperfect (*terminaba*, *duraba*) for what happened again and again or lasted a while, and the preterite (*terminó*, *atacaron*) for one event. *Mientras* needs an action that lasts: you cannot say *mientras lo atacaron*.
